answer: A verifiable delay function (VDF) can gate identity creation: each new agent must finish a sequential computation that takes a fixed wall-clock time and cannot be sped up by parallel hardware, like a nebula that only condenses at its own pace. An attacker at the nadir of cheap identity farming still faces one long sequential delay per fake identity, so spawning ten thousand Sybils costs ten thousand hours of chained work, not one burst of compute. A hollow identity minted in seconds is impossible; the delay makes mass forgery slow, measurable, and pointless.
